summary: Round 3, prose only (ADR-0044, an ADR-0043 Status amendment plus two body corrections, revision banners on research docs 04/10/13, corrected javadoc on SubscriptionEvent and SubscriptionEventGrantTest, M5.66, M5.45f done). No production logic, no wire change, no object-store request added, moved or authorised anywhere in this diff; the only src/main edit is javadoc. THE FOUR ROUND-2 FINDINGS I CHECKED FIRST ARE EACH SUBSTANTIVELY FIXED. r2-1: doc 13 now carries a banner at :105-113 and the sweep row at :248 says so, naming the two hits the earlier draft mis-dispositioned and stating that a false 'confirmed' is worse than an omission; doc 03:153 is a separate row as a third structure. r2-2: doc 10 §7:182 carries its own banner. r2-3: ADR-0043's two 'no owner' sentences are corrected in place at :120-124 and :218-224. r2-4: the arithmetic is now measured and I re-derived all of it independently. THE MEASUREMENT CHECKS OUT: the two golden files are 128 and 123 bytes on disk, and GoldenSubscriptionEventTest's two factories differ in nothing but (4096, 65536) versus RANGE_ABSENT, so the 5-byte delta really is the two uvarints (4096 -> 2 bytes, 65536 -> 3); encode writes a presence byte unconditionally in v3 (SubscriptionEvent :76-86), so 6 bytes for the fixture and 7 at the modelled shape is right; 11,200/8,388,608 = 0.1335%, 2,800/8,388,608 = 0.033%, 7/128 = 5.47%, 1,600x128 = 204,800 = 2.441%, and 0.1335/2.4414 = 5.47% = ~41x. Every counted fact in the Context table is true, read rather than taken: no src/main backend names presign, every SubscriptionTransport implementation in the tree is under src/test or src/clusterTest, M1.11b is todo, client/build.gradle.kts declares exactly api(project(':format')), check-module.sh:234 NO_HTTP is 'format binstore-spi sequencer ingest' and :236 NO_CLOUD is 'client plugin', check-io-seam.sh:58 exempts exactly binstore-backends, research 02-cost-model.md:299 is R12 at ~19.5 KiB while cost.md has no R12 at all, and SubscriptionHub:446-452 does carry the comment the Consequences section says it does. BUT THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION I WAS ASKED IS STILL YES, AND THE CLEAREST INSTANCE IS A FILE NO ROUND HAS NAMED: docs/research/50-open-questions.md Q8 asserts the exact claim the doc 10 §8 banner retires -- 'Every event carries coordinates even when it also carries inline bytes, so a subscriber can always fall back' -- and it appears in no row of the sweep table, in the one file AGENTS.md calls the decision log where 'every question is answered'. Two more corrections landed in one of two places: ADR-0043's new Status line states that security.md rule 3's range half is CLOSED, which ADR-0044 Decision (c):125 exists to deny in its own heading; and ADR-0044's alternative (b1) still rejects the closest call in the record by citing doc 04 §2c and doc 10 §7 as live corpus design, both banner-retired by this same commit, with the sweep table at :243 documenting that fact instead of fixing it.

findings.title: Q8 of the corpus decision log asserts the claim the doc 10 §8 banner retires, carries no banner, and is absent from the sweep table
findings.summary: 50-open-questions.md:45-46 reads 'Every event carries coordinates even when it also carries inline bytes, so a subscriber can always fall back.' That is word for word the claim ADR-0044 retires in Consequences and banners at doc 10 §8: 'Because every event carries coordinates regardless of mode, every mode can degrade to every other mode.' The banner this commit writes says the conclusion survives and the reason does not -- degradation is served by the segment's own directory, and the event's copies are read by nobody. Q8 gives the same wrong reason for the same right conclusion, in a file whose header reads 'every question raised during the research phase is now decided' and 'Last updated: 2026-08-30'. It carries no revision banner anywhere near Q8 (grepped: the file's only three warning marks are at :75, :110 and :155, on unrelated paragraphs). It matches the sweep's own 'coordinates' pattern -- the pattern added to the list this round precisely because a non-matching hit was called a miss -- and it appears in no row of the table at ADR-0044:233-251.
findings.failure_scenario: AGENTS.md routes every agent to this file by name: '50-open-questions.md is the decision log: every question is answered', and the research skill's routing table sends the question 'can we drop a field from the event' straight there. M5.66's owner -- the row this commit creates to decide whether byteStart/byteLen come off the wire -- opens Q8, finds a DECIDED question stating that the coordinates are what lets a subscriber fall back, and concludes the fields are load-bearing for the tier-2 fallback and cannot be removed. That closes M5.66's second arm on a reason ADR-0044 has already killed, and the sweep table gives them no way to notice: an absent row is, in criterion 3's own words, indistinguishable from 'not looked at'. It is the round-1 blocking finding (doc 04 §2c omitted) and the round-2 finding (doc 10 §7 left standing) a third time, one document over, and this one is the page the tooling points at first.
findings.suggested_fix: One banner under Q8 and one table row. The banner: the conclusion (push is best-effort, a dropped event costs latency only) survives; the reason does not -- a subscriber falls back through the COMMIT CHAIN and the segment's own directory, not through the event's byteStart/byteLen, which no reader in the tree consumes and which M5.66 owns. Same text the doc 10 §8 banner already carries.

findings.title: The new Status line says security.md rule 3's range half is CLOSED; ADR-0044 Decision (c) is headed 'is NOT closed'
findings.summary: ADR-0043:8-9 now reads 'The reopening under Decision (b) below is CLOSED by that record, and so is security.md rule 3's range half, which ADR-0044 Decision (c) hands to M5.66'. 'and so is' attaches to CLOSED, and the trailing clause does not rescue it -- handing a clause to a row is precisely not closing it. ADR-0044:125 is headed '(c) security.md rule 3's range half is NOT closed, and it now has an owner', and :128-131 spells out why that distinction is the point: answering (a) and (b) without it 'would leave the chain reading ADR-0043 -> M5.45f -> done with the standard's clause marked settled having never been addressed, which is worse than leaving it visibly open'. The two body corrections this same commit makes at :120-124 and :218-224 get it right -- 'gives it to M5.66, which owns whether a range ever becomes fillable'. Only the Status block, the newest text and the first a reader meets, says closed.
findings.failure_scenario: This is the r2-3 audit path with the answer flipped. ADR-0041:114 defers rule 3's range half and hands off through this record, so the next security pass -- or M5.20's sweep -- opens ADR-0043, reads the amendment banner at the top rather than scrolling 115 lines to the body, and records rule 3 as satisfied by ADR-0044. The clause is in fact open: the grant is scoped to a key and to no range, and M5.66 is todo and may discharge it either by building a bounded read or by declining it with a reason. A standard's clause marked settled having never been addressed is exactly the state ADR-0044 calls worse than leaving it open, and it is now asserted in the one place an auditor of that clause lands first. It is also the one-of-two-places defect inside the fix for the one-of-two-places defect: the body moved to 'owned', the Status line moved to 'closed'.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the sentence: 'The reopening under Decision (b) below is CLOSED by that record. security.md rule 3's range half is NOT -- ADR-0044 Decision (c) leaves it open and gives it an owner, M5.66, whose criterion 4 names the rule and the standard.' The body sentences at :120-124 and :218-224 already say it this way.

findings.title: Alternative (b1) still rejects the closest call in the record by citing two corpus lines this same commit banner-retires; the sweep table documents that instead of fixing it
findings.summary: :176-178 reads 'The corpus also designed for ranges throughout (doc 04 §2c, doc 10 §7's "merge adjacent ranges before requesting, in every mode"), so removal is a larger overturn than one row should make.' Both citations are retired by banners this commit writes. doc 04 §2c's new banner at :222-235 retires three claims by name including 'the coordinates let a node union its runs into one ranged GET'. doc 10 §7:182's new banner says in its first line 'the COALESCING stands, the RANGES do not'. So the reason given for not removing the fields is that the corpus designed for ranges, in the record whose Decision (b) establishes that no range is expressible and whose own banners strike those two lines. The sweep row at :243 acknowledges this in present tense -- 'alternative (b1) below quotes this very line as live corpus design ... it is the one-of-two-places defect a fifth time in this family' -- and then leaves (b1) unchanged, 67 lines above the table and read first.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's criterion 3 requires its owner to revisit Decision (b), so they read (b1), the paragraph that weighs keep-versus-remove and is labelled 'the closest call in this record'. The third reason offered is that the corpus designed for ranges throughout, with two citations. They follow them, find both banner-retired by the very ADR they are reading, and cannot tell whether the record knew: either they discount the whole rejection, or they take the corpus's range design as live evidence against removal and keep a field the same record says no reader consumes. The two-format-changes-against-zero argument in the preceding sentence survives on its own -- which is why this is major rather than blocking -- but a rejection standing partly on citations the record itself strikes is not a rejection a later reader can re-weigh, and re-weighing is what criterion 3 obliges them to do.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut or invert the sentence: the corpus's range design is what this record retires, so it is not evidence for keeping the fields. If the intended point is that the corpus expected ranges to become expressible, say that and cite M5.66 rather than two banner-retired lines. Then the :243 sweep row can say 'corrected' about (b1) as well as about §7.

findings.title: The paragraph that weighs keep-versus-remove, and the Consequences line, still price the decision at 0.13% alone after :111 says the decision is taken on the larger figure
findings.summary: :111 states 'THE DECISION IS TAKEN ON THE LARGER FIGURE.' The two places where the decision is actually weighed name only the smaller one: :174, in (b1), 'at **0.13%** of the segment they describe, keeping them is close to free'; and :208, in Consequences, '(b) keeps the bounded read possible at a cost of 0.13%' -- bare, with no denominator at all, which is the form round 2's own minor r2-6 said 'turns from deprecated into wrong if finding M5.45f-r2-4 is fixed'. r2-4 is fixed. ADR-0043:6-7's new amendment banner is a third site carrying 0.13% alone ('prices it at 0.13% of the segment'). The javadoc at SubscriptionEvent:121-124 and M5.66's backlog row both carry the pair correctly, which is what makes these three stand out.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader skimming Consequences for what (b) cost reads '0.13%' with no denominator in the record that spent a paragraph establishing that the denominator is the whole question, and carries away the figure the record deprecates. Minor rather than major because 'of the segment they describe' at :174 is an accurate qualification, the corrected pair sits 60 lines above under an emphatic heading in the same section, and the decision does not flip at either figure -- 5.5% of a 128-byte event is still small.
findings.suggested_fix: Under rule 11 this is probably best recorded in the commit body and left. If touched, touch all three at once -- :174, :208 and ADR-0043:6-7 -- so the price reads the same wherever the decision is weighed.

findings.title: The consistency check does not hold at the digits it shows, and 7/128 mixes a modelled numerator with a measured denominator
findings.summary: Two arithmetic points in the paragraph that exists to be checkable. (1) :110-111 reads '1,600 events x 128 bytes is 204,800 bytes, **2.4%** of the segment, and 0.13 / 2.44 = 5.5%'. 0.13 / 2.44 = 5.33%, not 5.5%. The identity holds only on the unrounded values -- 0.1335 / 2.4414 = 5.47% -- so the check as displayed does not reproduce, in the one paragraph whose stated purpose is 'the check that the earlier pair failed'. (2) :105's '7 / 128' takes the numerator from the modelled 8 MiB / 1,600-run shape (byteStart 4 uvarint bytes + byteLen 2 + flag 1) and the denominator from the measured fixture, whose own range costs 6 bytes (two varints of 5 plus the flag) on 128 -- 4.7%. At the modelled shape the event is 129 bytes and the figure is 5.4%. All three round to 'about 5.5%' and nothing in the decision turns on it; the defect is that a reader re-deriving it gets a different number twice and cannot tell whether that is rounding or a third error in a paragraph that has already had one.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.66's criterion 1 requires its owner to derive a crossover number, and :115-116 tells them to derive their own rather than reach for these -- so they will re-do this arithmetic to see how it was done. They get 5.3% from the displayed division and 4.7% from the measured fixture, against the 5.5% the record asserts, and either re-open the price or spend a round establishing that the gap is rounding. Minor: the decision is taken on the larger figure either way, and 4.7% and 5.5% argue identically.
findings.suggested_fix: Show the division on the unrounded values -- 0.1335 / 2.4414 = 5.5% -- and say which shape each term comes from: 6 bytes on the 128-byte fixture is 4.7%, 7 bytes on the 129-byte modelled event is 5.4%, and 5.5% is the round figure both support.

findings.title: Three propagated sites call a modelled number 'measured'; what was measured is 128 against 123
findings.summary: doc 04 §2c's banner at :235 says 'ADR-0044 keeps the coordinates at a measured 7 bytes per event'; doc 13's banner at :112 says 'keeps the fields at a measured 5.5% of the subscription stream'; the backlog M5.45f cell at :67 says 'at a MEASURED 7 bytes per event'. Neither 7 nor 5.5% was measured. The measurement is the two golden files, 128 against 123, giving 5 varint bytes for that fixture and 6 with the flag. 7 is derived at an assumed shape -- 8 MiB, ~1,600 runs, byteStart reaching 8,388,608 for 4 uvarint bytes, byteLen averaging 5.2 KiB for 2 -- and ADR-0044 itself is careful about this, writing '7 at the 8 MiB / 1,600-run shape **modelled** above' at :99-100. Only the three propagated copies drop the distinction.
findings.failure_scenario: Non-negotiable 4's territory, in the round that exists because a number was asserted rather than measured. A reader of the corpus banner -- routed there for exactly the M5.66 question -- takes 7 bytes per event as an empirical figure and reuses it at a different segment shape, where it is wrong in both terms: byteStart's uvarint width tracks segment size and byteLen's tracks runs per segment, so a 64 MiB segment or a 200-run one gives a different number. ADR-0044:115-116 already tells M5.66 to derive its own, which is why this is minor.
findings.suggested_fix: One word in each of the three: 'a modelled 7 bytes per event (measured at 5 varint bytes in the golden fixture)', and in doc 13 'a modelled ~5.5%'.

findings.title: A third ownership sentence in ADR-0043 still conditions M5.45g's seam signature on M5.45f, which this commit marks done
findings.summary: :231 reads 'AND M5.45g's SEAM TAKES NO RANGE PARAMETER UNTIL M5.45f SAYS ONE CAN BE FILLED'. M5.45f is marked done in this diff and answered 'not today', with M5.66 owning whether one ever becomes fillable. The Status block at :10-11 says 'the body is left standing ... with the two ownership sentences marked in place' -- and the two marked are :120-124 and :218-224. This is a third, in the same file, in the paragraph a reader of M5.45g will land on because it is the one about M5.45g's signature.
findings.failure_scenario: M5.45g is todo and is the next row in this family. Its taker reads ADR-0043 for the seam's shape, finds the signature conditioned on a row that is done, and has to reconstruct from the M5.45f cell whether done means the range was granted or refused. The answer they need -- no range today, M5.66 decides -- is two other places in the same file and in ADR-0044. Nothing breaks; it costs a lookup, which is why this is minor and not the same finding as the Status line.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark it like the other two: '...UNTIL M5.66 SAYS ONE CAN BE FILLED -- M5.45f answered that none can be filled today (ADR-0044 Decision (b)).'
